edges.description: Proposed rather than demonstrated. A published model argues that raised cytosolic calcium in mania drives increased mitochondrial respiration and ATP production, with the euthymic and depressive phases showing the opposite. No study cited here measures calcium and mitochondrial respiration in the same subjects across a mood transition, so the edge is recorded at unknown-intermediate directness.
intermediate_mechanisms: Raised cytosolic calcium is proposed to stimulate oxidative phosphorylation, in part through modulation of the F1-FO elements of ATP synthase, alongside oxidative stress and pro-inflammatory cytokine signaling that are themselves higher in mania.

edges.description: Clock-gene disruption raises dopaminergic output. Evidence is a targeted rodent perturbation; no human circadian variant has been shown to drive dopaminergic change in bipolar patients, so the edge is model-organism grounded rather than established in human disease.
intermediate_mechanisms: Loss of CLOCK function in ventral tegmental area dopaminergic neurons alters expression of ion channels and dopamine-related genes, increasing the firing activity of those neurons and so raising dopaminergic drive to forebrain reward circuits.

GSK-3β phosphorylates core clock proteins, so excess GSK-3β activity shortens/destabilizes circadian period and amplitude (lithium's GSK-3β inhibition lengthens period, per the GSK3β-haploinsufficiency model).
Excess GSK-3β activity suppresses BDNF/neurotrophic and β-catenin survival signaling, impairing synaptic plasticity in fronto-limbic mood circuits.

edges.limitations: Six patients, all white men with bipolar I disorder recruited from lithium monotherapy trials, and one neuron type. The hyperexcitability was seen in three-week-old neurons and reversed as the neurons aged. No experiment shows that it causes mood episodes. Fidelity is MODERATE because the cells are patient-derived and human, but the finding has not been matched to a measurement in patients' brains.

nodes.description: Glycogen synthase kinase-3β (GSK-3β) is a constitutively active serine/threonine kinase that phosphorylates β-catenin, tau, and numerous circadian and pro-apoptotic substrates. Excess GSK-3β activity is implicated in bipolar mood instability, and GSK-3β is the principal molecular target through which lithium is thought to exert its mood-stabilizing and neuroprotective effects. Lithium inhibits GSK-3β both directly (Mg2+-competitive) and indirectly (via the Akt / β-arrestin-2 / PP2A axis), stabilizing β-catenin and mimicking canonical Wnt signaling.

nodes.description: Altered intracellular calcium handling is among the oldest and most replicated cellular findings in bipolar disorder: basal and stimulated cytosolic calcium are elevated in patient platelets and lymphocytes, and endoplasmic-reticulum calcium release through the IP3 receptor is enhanced in patient lymphoblasts carrying the low-expressing BCL2 rs956572 AA genotype. This is the cellular counterpart of the calcium-channel genetics curated under CACNA1C. Two scope limits are load-bearing and should not be read past: the replicated measurements are in peripheral blood cells rather than neurons, and they have not been shown to track mood state over time -- the original series found little correlation between calcium measures and mood-rating severity. The node therefore records a trait-associated calcium abnormality, not a demonstrated driver of episode switching (see the attached knowledge gap).

nodes.description: Patient-derived neurons show intrinsic hyperexcitability, offering a cellular endophenotype that sits between the ion-channel genetics and the circuit-level findings. iPSC-derived hippocampal dentate-gyrus-like granule neurons from bipolar patients fire action potentials hyperactively and carry mitochondrial abnormalities relative to control-derived neurons. The finding is also a treatment-response stratifier: lithium reverses the hyperexcitability only in neurons from donors who were themselves clinical lithium responders. Scope limits -- six manic bipolar I donors and four unaffected individuals, one differentiated neuron type, and no demonstration that hyperexcitability causes episode switching rather than marking trait vulnerability.

nodes.description: Overactivity of the phosphatidylinositol (PIP2 / IP3) second-messenger cycle is implicated in bipolar mood instability (the "inositol depletion hypothesis"). The cycle regenerates free myo-inositol through inositol monophosphatase (IMPase) and inositol polyphosphate 1-phosphatase; lithium uncompetitively inhibits these Mg2+-dependent phosphatases, depleting free inositol and dampening the overactive signaling — a therapeutic target shared with valproate and carbamazepine. (The disease-state direction shown here is the overactive baseline; lithium's opposing, inhibitory action is captured on the Lithium treatment's target_mechanisms edge.)
